name: WELLS, the Hon. Anika Shay

headline.note: Official ministerial and first-person sources establish private legal work at Maurice Blackburn from 2014 to the 2019 election. Public professional biographies also report five years as a federal Labor government adviser before that role, but do not identify the employing office, dates, hours or leave. Political staff and elected office are excluded, and the private legal role lacks substantive full-time evidence. No public/private full-time headline total is calculable.

career_spells.employer: Residential aged-care facility, employer not identified
career_spells.evidence_note: A biographical profile reports that Wells worked part-time at the residential aged-care facility where her mother worked. The employer, dates, role, ownership, hours and leave are not identified.
career_spells.counting_note: The part-time work is retained as an unresolved early employment lead; no sector or duration can be calculated.

career_spells.employer: Griffith University and Australian National University
career_spells.role: Bachelor of Laws (Honours), Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and Government, and Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice student
career_spells.evidence_note: The official ministerial biography records the Griffith degrees. Public biographies also record an Australian National University graduate diploma and admission to legal practice in 2012. Exact enrolment and completion dates and study/employment overlaps are not published.

career_spells.employer: Australian Government ministerial office or offices, not identified
career_spells.evidence_note: Public professional biographies report five years as a Labor adviser in the federal government before Wells joined Maurice Blackburn in 2014. They do not identify the office or offices, titles, exact boundaries, hours or leave. A start year is therefore not inferred from the stated duration.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded from the public/private headline totals.

career_spells.role: Lawyer specialising in workers' compensation and road-injury matters
career_spells.evidence_note: The official ministerial biography records legal work at Maurice Blackburn from 2014 to 2019. Wells' first speech describes private-sector workers' compensation practice, and party biographies add representation of people injured at work or on the road. The exact commencement, payroll cessation, hours, leave and campaign arrangements are not published; 18 May 2019 is an outer bound from election, not a proved employment endpoint.
career_spells.counting_note: Private legal employment is supported, but exact boundaries and substantive full-time evidence are insufficient.

career_spells.evidence_note: A 2020 profile says Wells co-founded the local Chermside parkrun in mid-2015. It describes community volunteering, not paid employment; a cessation date is not supplied.

career_spells.role: Member of the House of Representatives for Lilley
career_spells.evidence_note: The official ministerial biography records election for Lilley in 2019 and re-election in 2022; the frozen Parliamentary Handbook records continuing service and subsequent re-election in 2025.
